title: Detect Binge Session Gaps Per User
prompt: You are analyzing viewer behavior for a streaming video platform. The `watch_events` table logs when each user starts watching an episode, recording the user, episode ID, and timestamp. A "binge session" is defined as consecutive episodes watched within 2 hours of each other; if a user waits more than 2 hours before their next episode, that starts a new session. Write a query that returns one row per watch event showing the `user_id`, `episode_id`, `watch_started_at`, and two calculated columns: `minutes_since_last_episode` (the number of minutes between this event's `watch_started_at` and the previous event's `watch_started_at` for the same user, or NULL for the user's first watch) and `new_session_flag` (a boolean that is TRUE if this event starts a new binge session—either it's the user's first watch or more than 120 minutes have elapsed since the last watch—and FALSE otherwise). Order the result by `user_id`, then `watch_started_at`.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE watch_events (user_id INTEGER NOT NULL, episode_id VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, watch_started_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL);

composite_moves: LAG(watch_started_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watch_started_at)
CASE to set boolean flag > 120 minutes or NULL

hints: You need to compare each row's timestamp to the previous row's timestamp within the same user's history.

Use LAG() with PARTITION BY user_id and ORDER BY watch_started_at to retrieve the previous watch timestamp. Remember to handle the case where there is no previous event (the first watch for each user).

Calculate the difference in minutes using EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (current_timestamp - lag_timestamp)) / 60. The new_session_flag is TRUE when minutes_since_last_episode IS NULL OR minutes_since_last_episode > 120.
answer_key: SELECT user_id, episode_id, watch_started_at, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (watch_started_at - LAG(watch_started_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watch_started_at))) / 60 AS minutes_since_last_episode, CASE WHEN LAG(watch_started_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watch_started_at) IS NULL OR EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (watch_started_at - LAG(watch_started_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watch_started_at))) / 60 > 120 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS new_session_flag FROM watch_events ORDER BY user_id, watch_started_at;

_meta.scenario: a streaming video service tracking watch time and binge depth
